items.title: [bug] command substitution is brace-expanded and executed once per alternative (duplicated side effects + corrupted output)
items.body:
## Summary

`hellish` applies **brace expansion to the raw source text of a command substitution**, and then **executes the command once per brace alternative**. `$(cmd '{a,b}')` runs `cmd` *twice* and concatenates the two outputs.

This is not just a quoting/word-splitting problem: single quotes do not protect the text, the substitution's **side effects are duplicated**, and the corruption happens even inside double quotes, where `"$(...)"` must always produce exactly one word.

## Version

```
hellish 2.3.2
Linux 5.15.0-185-generic x86_64
```

## Steps to reproduce

### 1. The command runs N times, once per alternative

This is the clearest demonstration — the appends are the side effect we count:

```console
$ hellish -c 'rm -f c; echo "$(printf "run\n" >> c; echo "{a,b}")" >/dev/null; wc -l < c'
2

$ bash -c 'rm -f c; echo "$(printf "run\n" >> c; echo "{a,b}")" >/dev/null; wc -l < c'
1
```

Three alternatives run it three times:

```console
$ hellish -c 'rm -f c; echo "$(printf "r\n" >> c; echo "{a,b,c}")" >/dev/null; wc -l < c'
3

$ bash -c 'rm -f c; echo "$(printf "r\n" >> c; echo "{a,b,c}")" >/dev/null; wc -l < c'
1
```

With no braces present, it correctly runs once, so the trigger is specifically the brace list in the substitution's source text.

### 2. The visible result is corrupted too

```console
$ hellish -c 'echo "$(echo "{a,b}")"'
a b

$ bash -c 'echo "$(echo "{a,b}")"'
{a,b}
```

That the outputs are *concatenated with a space* — rather than the string simply being split — is confirmed by giving the command a suffix:

```console
$ hellish -c 'echo "$(printf "%s-END" "{a,b}")"'
a-END b-END          # two runs: "a-END" and "b-END"

$ bash -c 'echo "$(printf "%s-END" "{a,b}")"'
{a,b}-END
```

If this were mere word-splitting of a single run's output, the result would be `a-ENDb-END`.

### 3. Single quotes do not protect the text

```console
$ hellish -c "echo \"\$(echo '{a,b}')\""
a b

$ bash -c "echo \"\$(echo '{a,b}')\""
{a,b}
```

### 4. Real-world case: an ordinary awk one-liner

`BEGIN{ printf "%d", 20 }` is itself a brace list as far as this bug is concerned, so awk is invoked twice, each time with half a program:

```console
$ hellish -c 'echo "[$(awk "BEGIN{ printf \"%d\", 20 }")]"'
awk: cmd. line:1: BEGIN printf "%d"
awk: cmd. line:1:       ^ syntax error
awk: cmd. line:1: BEGIN 20
awk: cmd. line:1:       ^ syntax error
[] []

$ bash -c 'echo "[$(awk "BEGIN{ printf \"%d\", 20 }")]"'
[20]
```

The two separate awk error messages are the duplicated execution showing through.

## Expected behaviour

Brace expansion is the **first** expansion step and applies to text from the script source only. It must not be applied to the interior of a command substitution as a unit, the command must be executed exactly **once**, and `"$(...)"` must yield exactly one word, verbatim — matching bash in every transcript above.

## Scope

Affected — every substitution form, quoted or not:

```console
$ hellish -c 'echo "$(echo "{a,b}")"'     # → a b
$ hellish -c 'echo $(echo "{a,b}")'       # → a b
$ hellish -c 'echo "`echo "{a,b}"`"'      # → a b   (backticks too)
```

Not affected — brace text that never passes through a substitution's source:

```console
$ hellish -c 'echo "{a,b}"'                                  # {a,b}  OK
$ hellish -c "echo '{a,b}'"                                  # {a,b}  OK
$ hellish -c 'v="{a,b}"; echo "$v"'                          # {a,b}  OK
$ hellish -c 'v="$(echo "{a,b}")"; echo "$v"'                # {a,b}  OK — assignment path is fine
$ hellish -c 'printf "{a,b}\n" > f; echo "$(cat f)"'         # {a,b}  OK — braces come from data, not source
$ hellish -c 'set -- "{a,b}"; echo "$1"'                     # {a,b}  OK
$ hellish -c 'export V="{a,b}"; sh -c "echo \$V"'            # {a,b}  OK
```

Note the contrast between the last two "OK" cases and the failures: when the brace text arrives as *data* (from a file, a variable, `read`) it is handled correctly. Only literal braces in the substitution's own source text trigger it. Assigning the substitution to a variable (`v=$(...)`) is a working workaround.

## Impact

- **Duplicated side effects.** Any `$( )` whose body writes a file, appends a log, increments a counter, sends a request, or removes something will do it twice or more. This can corrupt data with no error shown.
- **Silent output corruption.** `"$(...)"` is *the* idiom for "capture this exactly". Anything handling awk/sed programs, JSON (`{"a", "b"}`), `find -exec` fragments, or C/C++ initialiser text is quietly wrong.
- No error, no non-zero exit status — it fails silently.

---
*Found while running the ft_irc project's shell test suite under both `bash` and `hellish` and diffing the output. Supersedes the mechanism described in the first revision of this issue: the defect is duplicated execution of the substitution, not rescanning of its output.*

items.title: Metal 2.0 port: data_movement/untilize — IdenticalNDShard factory (borrowed-DFB validator prerequisite)
items.body:
Port the remaining `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` of `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/untilize` to Metal 2.0 / Host 2.0 APIs (Gen1 WH/BH target).

Parent: #41908
Follow-up to: #53583 (6 of 7 factories ported)

## Scope
Only the **input-and-output ND-shard-identical** factory of `UntilizeDeviceOperation`:
- `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` (`device/factories/untilize_multi_core_input_and_output_nd_shard_type_and_shard_spec_identical_program_factory.cpp`)
  - kernels: `eltwise/unary/device/kernels/dataflow/reader_unary_sharded.cpp`, `data_movement/sharded/device/kernels/dataflow/writer_unary_sharded.cpp`, and `device/kernels/compute/untilize_variable_num_blocks.cpp` — all three already have `_metal2` forks created in #53583.

The other six factories are done (ported in #53583). The op runs mixed today — `select_program_factory` dispatches identical input+output ND-shard specs to this legacy `create_descriptor` factory, and per-factory dispatch keeps the op building and running. **This is the only remaining GREEN-subset factory.**

## Why this was deferred (blocker)
A faithful port — both input and output CBs are borrowed-memory (`CBDescriptor::buffer` set) → borrowed-memory DFBs via `DataflowBufferSpec::borrowed_from`, sized exactly as the legacy backed-CB `total_size` (`num_shards_per_core_in_group_1 × tile-padded-shard-tiles × tile_size`) — is rejected by the Metal 2.0 **spec validator** on **uneven ND sharding**.

`tt_metal/impl/metal2_host_api/program_spec.cpp:1567` enforces a *coarse* spec-time check `dfb_bytes <= tensor_spec.compute_packed_buffer_size_bytes()`, comparing the uniform per-node DFB size against the **whole logical packed tensor** size. For a heavily padded uneven shard the per-core DFB can exceed the whole logical tensor. Concrete failing case: tensor `[4,128,160]` bf16, shard `[3,96,96]`, 3-core grid → per-core DFB `3 shards × 27 tiles × 2048 = 165888 B` vs whole packed tensor `80 tiles × 2048 = 163840 B` — over by exactly one tile. The code comment there acknowledges this coarse check is imprecise for sharded tensors (the *precise* per-bank check runs later in `AttachBorrowedDFBBuffers`, `program_run_args.cpp`), but the coarse check is a hard `TT_FATAL`. **Even** ND-shard cases pass.

Failing test: `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/data_movement/test_untilize.py::test_untilize_nd_shard_to_same_shard_spec_uneven_input_shard_spec` (4 parametrizations).

## What needs to happen
1. **Metal 2.0 framework fix (prerequisite, separate track):** relax the spec-time coarse borrowed-DFB size check for L1-sharded `borrowed_from` TensorSpecs — defer wholly to the per-bank attach-time check in `AttachBorrowedDFBBuffers`, or compare against the sharded per-core allocation rather than the logical packed size. Owner: Metal 2.0 framework team.
2. **Re-audit + port** `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` to `create_program_artifacts` (`ProgramSpecFactoryConcept`) once the framework fix lands. The conversion is otherwise mechanical (borrowed-memory DFBs via `borrowed_from`, named `dfb::`/`args::`, the `untilize_variable_num_blocks_metal2` fork already exists) — it was written and reverted during #53583, so the diff is known.

## Notes / instructions
- WH/BH only — no Quasar emulation.
- **Do NOT hand-tune the borrowed-DFB size to pass the coarse check** — buffer size is a correctness property in the tilize/untilize sharded family and hand-tuning it risks silent data corruption (cf. #51305).

items.title: [BugFix] Drop corrupted local cache when tablet merge sstable rebuild hits corruption
items.body:
## Why I'm doing:

Follow-up to #77481, closing the last high-risk gap found in the PK index sstable read-path audit. The tablet-merge legacy sstable rebuild paths read every entry of the source tablets' PK index sstables with neither checksum verification nor the drop-corrupted-cache fallback:

- A corrupted local cache copy of a source sstable makes the merge fail on every retry that lands on the same node — the same wedge #77481 fixed for PK index compaction (the cache is persistent, so nothing ever invalidates the bad blocks).
- Worse, without checksum verification a corrupted-but-still-decodable block can be **silently rebuilt into the merged tablet's index** with wrong (rssid, rowid) values — a correctness hazard, not just availability.

## What I'm doing:

In `be/src/storage/lake/tablet_merger.cpp`, for both rebuild paths (`rebuild_legacy_shared_sstable` and `rebuild_non_shared_legacy_sstable`):

- Add `drop_source_sstable_cache_on_corruption(...)`: on a `Corruption` status it increments `pk_index_sst_read_error_total`, logs a WARNING, drops the source sstable's local cache via the existing `drop_corrupted_sstable_cache()` (gated by `lake_clear_corrupted_cache_data`, same as #77481), and propagates the original status. Unlike compaction's merged iterator, the rebuild knows exactly which file it is reading, so only that one file's cache is dropped.
- Wire the handler into every sst-read failure exit: the iterator status check after the scan loop (both functions), the early status check after `SeekToFirst` (non-shared), and the value protobuf parse failures — which are also reclassified from `InternalError` to `Corruption` (the bytes come straight out of the sstable's data block), matching the `KeyValueMerger::merge` change in #77481.
- Opening the source sstable already self-heals via `PersistentIndexSstable::init`'s internal drop-and-retry; behavior on success paths is unchanged.
- Checksum verification for these rebuild reads (so corrupted-but-still-decodable blocks cannot be silently rebuilt into the merged index) is added by #77479, gated by the `lake_pk_index_sst_verify_checksum` config it introduces; this PR carries only the self-healing half, so the two PRs stay independent and can merge in any order.

UT (in `tablet_reshard_test.cpp`, `USE_STAROS` guarded): two end-to-end cases — one through the shared-legacy rebuild route, one through the non-shared rebuild route — corrupt the first data block's compression-type byte of a real source sstable (footer/index stay intact so opening succeeds), run `publish_resharding_tablet`, and assert the merge fails with `Corruption` and the `PersistentIndexSstable::drop_corrupted_cache` sync point fired exactly once for the source file.

Backport note: only branch-4.1 carries the tablet merge/reshard rebuild paths; 4.0/3.5 do not have this code.

items.title: [Windows][zh-CN] Terminal tool corrupts native-program output (GBK → U+FFFD) — local.py _run_bash hardcodes encoding=utf-8 + errors=replace

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Chinese/Japanese Windows (system locale = ANSI code page GBK/cp936), the Hermes terminal tool **silently and irreversibly corrupts** output from native Windows programs (powershell.exe, cmd, taskkill, pnpm, etc.) that print localized messages in the ANSI codepage.

Instead of readable Chinese error text, the agent sees a wall of `�` (U+FFFD) replacement chars — the diagnostic value of the message is completely lost.

## Root Cause

`tools/environments/local.py` — `_run_bash()` (and `_popen_bash()` in `tools/environments/base.py`) hardcode:

```python
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    args, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", ...
)
```

Git-Bash passes through raw bytes from native Windows children unchanged. On a zh-CN system those bytes are GBK/cp936, not UTF-8. Decoding them as UTF-8 with `errors="replace"` emits U+FFFD for every byte — irreversible (the original bytes are discarded by `text=True` decoding at the pipe level).

MSYS tools (ls/cat/grep…) emit UTF-8 so they are fine; the bug hits **native Windows executables** invoked through bash.

## Repro (100% on zh-CN Windows 11 + Hermes\s bundled Git Bash)

Run via terminal tool:

```bash
powershell -NoProfile -Command "Stop-Process -Name no-such-process -ErrorAction Stop" 2>&1 || true`
```

Actual (Hermes mode — `text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`):

```
Stop-Process : �Ҳ�����Ϊ��no-such-process���Ľ��̡�����֤�ý������ƣ�Ȼ���ٴε��� cmdlet��
... (44 U+FFFD chars)
```

Expected: GBK-decoded message:

```
Stop-Process : 找不到名为“no-such-process”的进程。请验证该进程名称，然后再次调用 cmdlet。
```

Raw-bytes proof (captured from the same command):

```
b\xd5\xd2\xb2\xbb\xb5\xbd...  → GBK decodes to 找不到
```

## Impact

- Agent cannot read any error message from PowerShell/cmd/taskkill/pnpm on CJK Windows — worse, it may hallucinate from garbage text
- Real-world evidence: 8+ occurrences today, largest one contained **8439 U+FFFD** chars from a PowerShell error block
- This is the mirror-image of earlier GBK crash bugs (#57252, #83726, #83851): those crashed with UnicodeDecodeError; the live fix (hardcoding utf-8) traded a crash for silent unrecoverable data corruption

## Suggested Fix

Do not let `text=True` decode at the pipe level. Collect raw bytes, then decode with sniffing (try UTF-8 strict, fall back to the system ANSI codepage, e.g. `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)` on Windows):

```python
# pseudo — in _drain on Windows
chunk = os.read(fd, 4096)          # keep raw bytes
output.append(decoder.decode(chunk))  # decoder chosen by codepage sniff
```

Or: on Windows run bash with `-o pipefail` plus `chcp 65001` for cmd children. Either way `errors="replace"` must not be the only safety net — it permanently destroys bytes that a fallback codepage decode could have recovered.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (zh-CN), ANSI codepage 936/GBK
- Hermes: current main (git 8911e2e0e, 2026-08-18)
- Terminal tool local backend, embedded Git Bash

items.title: feat(dbt): Focus attendance and gradebook intermediate models
items.body:
# Pull Request

## Summary & Motivation

When merged, this pull request will add the three remaining Focus intermediate
models tracked in #4865, and the dlt ingestion the gradebook one needs.

`int_focus__attendance_day` and `int_focus__attendance_period` resolve Focus
attendance codes to readable titles and excused/tardy flags. These are what
#4803 needs to model Miami attendance from Focus directly, which that issue
names as the real fix for its 155,863 orphaned rows.

`int_focus__gradebook_grades` puts each gradebook score together with its
assignment, its category, that category's weight toward the final grade, and
the course period the score belongs to.

Getting a grade to its course period required ingesting two Focus tables that
were never configured for extraction. They exist in Focus, but nothing was
pulling them, so a gradebook grade had no path to a course. #4220 tracked
staging coverage of the tables we already pull, so it never surfaced this gap.

## Reviewer Notes

**The two attendance models resolve their codes differently, on purpose.**
`attendance_period` stores code ids. `attendance_day` stores a short name
(`U`, `AE`, `AD`), and short names repeat across schools and years, so that
model resolves the school from the marking period before joining. The two
joins look inconsistent side by side; they are not.

**A grade's course period is genuinely ambiguous, and the model resolves it

sections, so an assignment maps to many course periods while a grade names

today are in that position. The model keeps the section the student is
actually scheduled into.

**No `attendance_calendar` join, though #4865 asks for one.** Its `minutes`
column is the same sentinel value on every current row, so there is nothing

grain than these models have. The design document records how to scope the

Claude-assisted, human-directed. Design document:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-focus-attendance-gradebook-intermediates-design.md`.
Implementation plan:
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-focus-attendance-gradebook-intermediates.md`.

**This PR lands in two pushes.** The first carries the dlt config, the source
declarations, and both attendance intermediates. The two new gradebook staging
models and `int_focus__gradebook_grades` follow, after the branch deployment

**Measurements behind the design**, all taken 2026-08-18 against live data,
either in `dagster_kippmiami_dlt_focus` or by probing Focus Postgres from a
`kippmiami` code-server pod:

- `attendance_period.attendance_code` and `.attendance_teacher_code` resolve to
  `attendance_codes.id` with 0 orphans of 15,171 rows.
- `attendance_day.daily_code` resolves to `attendance_codes.short_name` scoped
  by year and school, 0 unresolved of 895 coded rows. `daily_pres_code` is null
  on every row. `state_value` is already the present/absent classification —
  6,804 of 7,699 rows are `daily_code is null` with `state_value = 1` — so the
  code join supplies the reason for an absence, not the classification.
- The assignment link has 428,009 rows over 355,583 distinct assignments;
  28,074 assignments map to more than one course period, including 11 of the 12
  that carry grades. Filtering by the student's schedule collapses every grade
  to exactly one course period, with 0 grades having a link row but no schedule
  match. 30 grades have no link row at all, which is why every join in that
  model is a LEFT join.
- `gradebook_assignment_types_join_course_periods` repeats an
  `(assignment_type_id, course_period_id)` pair 23,318 times — weights change
  per marking period — so the weight join keys on the triple including
  `marking_period_id`. 87,913 of its 89,206 rows carry `final_grade_percent`.
- `schedule` repeats a student and course-period pair on 299 combinations, so
  the model collapses it with `group by` and uses it as a lookup rather than
  joining it as a table. The earlier check counted distinct course periods and
  could not have caught this.
- `attendance_calendar.minutes` is `999` on all 7,697 matched 2026 rows;
  `bell_schedule_id` is populated on 544. Scoping to
  `attendance_calendars.default_calendar = 'Y'` reduces 1,554 duplicate
  `(syear, school_id, school_date)` keys to 177, all in `syear` 2016 — so the
  join is safe for current data, just not informative.

**Primary-key tests do not gate anything here.** All five models declare
`unique` and `not_null` at `severity: error`, matching the surrounding staging
models — but those resolve to `warn`. The root project sets
`data_tests: +severity: warn` in `src/dbt/kippmiami/dbt_project.yml`, and
root-project config outranks config declared inside an installed package, which
every `focus` model is. The manifest confirms it:
`unique_stg_focus__attendance_codes_id` resolves to `warn` despite its YAML
declaring `error`. This is pre-existing and repo-wide, not introduced here.

Consequence: a join that multiplied rows would warn, and the build would still
go green. Grain was therefore confirmed by direct count rather than inferred —
`int_focus__attendance_day` 7,701 rows and 7,701 distinct PK,
`int_focus__attendance_period` 15,633 / 15,633,
`int_focus__gradebook_grades` 697 / 697 against 697 staging rows,
`stg_focus__gradebook_assignments_join_course_periods` 428,025 / 428,025.
Whether the network wants that override lifted for primary-key tests is a
policy question this PR does not settle.

**One latent ambiguity is documented rather than fixed.** A grade resolves to a
single course period only while the student sits in exactly one of the
assignment's sections. Three student-and-assignment pairs currently match two
sections each; none carries a grade, so nothing duplicates today. Filtering the
match by assignment date against the schedule window was tested and rejected —
it drops a real grade belonging to a student added to a section on 2026-08-18
and back-graded on work assigned 2026-08-12, which is ordinary late-enrollment
behaviour. Trading a case that happens for one that has not seemed wrong. The
model description records this.

**Columns removed for carrying no signal.** `state_attendance_type` is null on
all 835 attendance codes, so `attendance_code_state_attendance_type` and
`daily_code_state_attendance_type` were dropped rather than mirrored onto the
teacher code as first suggested. `chronic_absenteeism` and `truancy` hold `Y`
on every code including `Present` — Focus config defaults, not classifications —
and `tardy` is null at day grain because `T` is period-level only, so all three
were dropped from `int_focus__attendance_day`. `daily_code_excused` stays; it
genuinely discriminates.

**Two traps worth knowing for anyone building on this locally.** The `focus`
project is a dbt package with `focus_schema: null` and no developer profile, so
it cannot be built standalone — build via `kippmiami`. And `--defer` falls back
to prod only for objects ABSENT from the dev schema, so a stale dev copy is
used silently and the model still builds green with wrong values. A 2026-06-22
copy of `stg_focus__attendance_codes` made 8 rows look unresolvable during
development. Both are recorded in the plan's Global Constraints.

Closes nothing on its own — #4865 also needs its body corrected, since it
states these models require no new ingestion.

Refs #4865
Refs #4803
Refs #3584

items.title: Enable MySQL/MariaDB strict mode so type errors fail loudly

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified and ready for an agent

items.body:
Follow-up flagged by #116 ("Out of scope here, but flag for a follow-up").

## Why

`config/database.php` sets `'strict' => false` for both the `mysql` and `mariadb` connections, so the session runs with `sql_mode = NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION`. That is what turned the shifted-XOVER bug in #116 from a type error into silent data corruption: a subject string written to `usenet_groups.last_record` was coerced to `0`, `2`, `5472`, or `18446744073709551615` instead of raising an error, and the affected groups stalled for a week before anyone noticed.

Verified on the production DB while diagnosing #116:

```
CAST('2O8W9UZ0… [3/10]' AS UNSIGNED) = 2
CAST('5472 - Some.Release' AS UNSIGNED) = 5472
CAST('kvTj34B5…' AS UNSIGNED) = 0
CAST('99999999999999999999999 hash' AS UNSIGNED) = 18446744073709551615
```

#116 fixed the specific write paths (the format cache, plus guards in `BinariesService`/`HeaderParser`), but every other unguarded write in the codebase still has the same silent-coercion behaviour available to it.

## What to look at

- Turn on `'strict' => true` (or at minimum `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`) for `mysql`/`mariadb` in `config/database.php`, ideally behind an env toggle with a documented default in `.env.example`.
- Sweep for writes that currently rely on lenient coercion — zero dates, over-long strings truncated on insert, out-of-range integers, and `''` written to numeric columns are the usual casualties.
- Run the full suite plus a real tmux processing cycle (binaries, backfill, releases, postprocess) against a strict-mode database before landing; this is a broad behavioural change and needs its own test pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- Strict mode (or `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`) is on for the MySQL/MariaDB connections, with the setting documented in `.env.example`.
- A full `tmux:start` cycle and the PHPUnit suite both run clean against a strict-mode database.
- Any write that strict mode exposes as a genuine bug is fixed rather than worked around by relaxing the mode again.

items.title: Review enabling MariaDB strict mode (sql_mode) — follow-up to #116 silent coercion

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue

items.body:
## Summary

Review enabling MySQL/MariaDB strict mode for the application's database connections. Follow-up from #116, where `'strict' => false` turned a type error (a header *Subject string* written into `usenet_groups.last_record`) into silent data corruption instead of a thrown `QueryException`.

This is a review/decision issue first: audit the impact, then decide between full strict, a targeted `sql_mode`, or leaving it and documenting why. It is **not** a blocker for #116 and does not change how #116 is implemented.

## Current state

- `config/database.php` sets `'strict' => false` on both the `mysql` (line 48) and `mariadb` (line 81) connections. Upstream NNTmux has carried `strict => false` since the original Laravel port (2017); no commit documents a reason.
- Effective session mode on prod (verified 2026-08-18): `sql_mode = NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION`, MariaDB 11.4.12.
- Consequence: out-of-range / non-numeric values are coerced with a warning nobody reads. Verified: `CAST('2O8W9UZ0… [3/10]' AS UNSIGNED) = 2`, `CAST('kvTj34B5…' AS UNSIGNED) = 0`, `CAST('99999999999999999999999 hash' AS UNSIGNED) = 18446744073709551615`, `CAST('-1' AS UNSIGNED) = 18446744073709551615`. In strict mode each of those `UPDATE`s would have raised `Incorrect integer value` / `Out of range value` and the binaries child process would have failed loudly on 2026-08-11 instead of a week later.

## What Laravel does with `strict => true`

For MySQL/MariaDB Laravel sets the session to:

```
ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY, STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, NO_ZERO_IN_DATE, NO_ZERO_DATE, ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO, NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION
```

(and `NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER` on older MySQL). `ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY` and the zero-date modes are the ones most likely to break legacy nZEDb-era queries and schema defaults, independent of the numeric-coercion problem that motivated this.

## Review scope

1. **Inventory lenient-coercion dependencies.** Places that may currently rely on non-strict behaviour:
   - Non-numeric / empty strings written to integer columns (grep raw `DB::update`/`DB::insert`/`->update([` with unvalidated request or NNTP-sourced values; `updateGroup()` in `app/Models/UsenetGroup.php` writes `first_record`/`last_record` straight from the admin form).
   - `'0000-00-00'` / `NULL`-less datetime defaults in old migrations (`NO_ZERO_DATE`, `NO_ZERO_IN_DATE`).
   - `GROUP BY` queries selecting non-aggregated columns (`ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY`) — the release/browse/search SQL in `app/Services/Search/`, `app/Services/Releases*`, admin stats, and the tmux monitor queries are the likely hits.
   - Division in SQL (`ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO`), e.g. completion-percentage expressions.
   - String values longer than the column (`Data too long`) — release names/subjects into `varchar(255)`.
2. **Run the full PHPUnit suite against a MariaDB instance** (not SQLite) with `strict => true`; SQLite ignores `sql_mode`, so the CI suite alone proves nothing here. `tests/Integration/` has MariaDB-backed tests to build on.
3. **Soak on prod with a rollback plan** — the tmux engine, queue workers, and admin pages exercise the write paths the tests don't. Enabling strict is a one-line config change; rollback is the same line.
4. **Decide** between:
   - **(a)** `'strict' => true` (full Laravel default set) — best long-term, highest audit cost.
   - **(b)** keep `'strict' => false` but set an explicit `'modes' => ['STRICT_TRANS_TABLES', 'NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION']` on both connections — makes bad numeric/string writes fail while leaving `ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY` and zero-date rules off. Small blast radius; directly prevents the #116 failure class.
   - **(c)** leave as-is and document why in `config/database.php` and `AGENTS.md`.
   Recommendation: start with **(b)** as the deliverable of this issue, treat **(a)** as a stretch once `ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY` violations are counted.
5. Whatever is chosen: record the decision as a rule (`.ai/rules`) and note it in `AGENTS.md` under Config so future writers know numeric writes will (or won't) throw.

## Relationship to #116

- #116's fixes (`getXOVER()` format-cache shape, guarded/validated `last_record` writes, `missed_parts` flood prevention, data repair) are **independent** of this issue and should land first. They validate at the application layer, so they are correct under either sql_mode.
- If strict mode is enabled later, nothing in #116 needs to change; the DB constraint just becomes a second line of defence behind the PHP validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written audit (in this issue) listing each category above with hit counts and the queries/paths that would break under `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES` and, separately, under the full Laravel strict set.
- Full suite green against MariaDB with the chosen mode; any code changes needed to get there are scoped as their own PR(s).
- Decision recorded in `config/database.php` comment + `AGENTS.md` + `.ai/rules`.

items.title: [cudax] Use _CCCL_NO_UNIQUE_ADDRESS instead of [[no_unique_address]]
items.body:
## Description

closes https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/issues/2358

cudax applied `[[no_unique_address]]` directly in five places. `_CCCL_NO_UNIQUE_ADDRESS` exists so the attribute is only emitted where it is known to be safe: it is empty on MSVC, whose implementation has caused silent runtime corruption when passing data into kernels, and under clang with nvcc in C++17, where cudafe++ does not honor it (nvbug 5265027). Switching these sites to the macro brings cudax in line with the rest of CCCL and removes the C4848 trigger from cudax's own code.

Sites changed:

| File | Sites |
| --- | --- |
| `__stf/internal/execution_policy.cuh` | 2 |
| `__stf/utility/run_once.cuh` | 1 |
| `__stf/internal/parallel_for_scope.cuh` | 1 |
| `__utility/optionally_static.cuh` | 1 |

A doc comment in `parallel_for_scope.cuh` that referenced the raw attribute was updated to name the macro. The one-line reformat in `optionally_static.cuh` is clang-format realigning `using __state_t` after the macro changed the declaration width.

No new includes were needed: all four headers already reach `<cuda/std/__cccl/attributes.h>` through `<cuda/__cccl_config>`, directly or via `<cuda/std/detail/__config>`.

`/wd4848` in `cudax/cmake/cudaxBuildCompilerTargets.cmake` is left in place, since MSVC still warns in cases local suppression cannot reach.

## Verification

- clang-format 22.1.5 (the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) is clean on all touched headers.
- `optionally_static.cuh` compiles clean host-side with clang at `-std=c++17` and `-std=c++20` under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.

**MSVC and CUDA verification is still needed.** This was developed without an MSVC toolchain or a CUDA-capable machine, so the MSVC build is unconfirmed locally and the three STF headers could not be compiled. CI should cover both.

Note that on MSVC and on clang+nvcc+C++17 these members no longer collapse, which is the intended effect of the macro but does change layout on those toolchains.

- [x] New or existing tests cover these changes. <!-- Existing cudax builds/tests cover this; no new behavior is introduced. -->
- [x] The documentation is up to date with these changes. <!-- No documented behavior changes. -->

items.title: fix(shtypes): harden MaybeString against escapes and non-scalar values
items.body:
Companion to #57 — the second half of making `shtypes` the one home for wire-coercion types.

### The problem

`MaybeString.UnmarshalJSON` is `strings.Trim(string(b), "\"")`. That strips quotes and nothing else:

- string escapes are never decoded — `"a\"b"` stores the raw escaped bytes
- `null` decodes to the literal text `null`
- a bool, array or object is **silently stringified** — a wire contract violation becomes quietly wrong data instead of an error

Downstream code noticed: the same hardened implementation has been written locally twice rather than trusting the exported type — one copy's doc comment says outright that it exists because *"the gosh helper does a naive strings.Trim"*.

### The change

Delegate to `encoding/json`: strings decode with escapes handled, numbers keep their textual form (`json.Number`), `null`/empty → `""`, anything else returns an `UnmarshalTypeError`. Plus `String()` and `Int()` accessors so call sites read naturally.

### Compatibility

- **Well-formed string/number values: identical behaviour.** That's the entire population observed on the wire.
- `null` now → `""` (was the text `null`) — strictly more useful.
- Non-scalars now **error** (were silently stringified) — this is the deliberate change; silence here is data corruption.
- gosh itself has **no non-test consumers** of `MaybeString`, so the blast radius inside this repo is zero.

### Tests

Both wire forms, big-number and float textual preservation, null/empty, escaped quote, unicode escape, and the four rejection shapes (`true`, `false`, `[1]`, `{"a":1}`) asserted to error rather than stringify. Accessors covered. Full suite green.

### Release note

If this and #56/#57 all merge, one v0.7.1 tag carries all three and downstream needs exactly one dependency bump.

items.title: fix(data): remap archetype ids on load so schema changes don't corrupt entities
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes a silent data-corruption class in persistence load: an archetype's id is its dense index in the `archetypes` array, written **by value** into the entity-location table. On load, archetypes are resolved by **identity** (component set + partition values), not by their serialized array position. So any schema change that adds, removes, or reorders an archetype resolves a persisted archetype to a *different live id* than the position it was saved at — and the never-remapped location-table indices then point entities at the **wrong archetype**. No throw, just wrong reads (a prior production incident class).

Two independent code paths had this bug:

1. **In-memory `Store`/`Core` snapshot restore** (`create-core.ts`) — `createStore(schema)` eagerly creates archetypes for every schema-declared archetype/resource *before* `fromData` runs, in declaration order, so ids desync from serialized positions whenever the declaration order changes.
2. **Incremental/journal persistence service** (`create-incremental-persistence-service.ts`) — `finalizeEntityLocationTable` pushed the raw on-disk manifest `archetypeId` straight into the restored location table with no translation, even though it already resolves the live archetype by name.

## Fix

- `core.fromData` resolves every persisted archetype **first**, building an `oldPosition → liveId` map, then translates the location table's stored ids through it via `remapSerializedArchetypeIds` — a pure transform co-located with the serialized-blob format (the generic `EntityLocationTable` interface is untouched).
- The persistence service writes the resolved `liveArchetype.id` (looked up by name from the manifest) instead of the stale on-disk id.

**No serialization format change** (ECS snapshot version stays `2`, manifest stays `1`): this is purely load-time reconciliation. Existing snapshots load correctly — and now correctly *under a schema change*.

## Tests

Added a red-first regression test per path, each reproducing the exact corruption (an entity saved in archetype A reads back as unrelated archetype B after a schema/plugin archetype is declared ahead of it), now green:

- `packages/data/src/ecs/store/public/create-store.test.ts`
- `packages/data-persistence/src/service/load-roundtrip.test.ts`

Full suites pass: **3055** data + **240** persistence tests; monorepo lint + typecheck clean.

items.title: hi3516ev300 + Winbond W25N01GV: silent data-pattern UBIFS rootfs corruption (kernel corrupts its own writes; NAND HW proven good) — hifmc100 ECC bug
items.body:
## Summary

On **hi3516ev300 + Winbond W25N01GV** SPI-NAND, the OpenIPC `nand-ultimate` build boots and mounts the UBIFS rootfs cleanly, but the **rootfs silently corrupts** over runtime. The failure is **data-pattern-specific** (always the same logical UBIFS block), **silent** (`ecc_failures=0`, `corrected_bits=0`), and — critically — **reproduces even when the running kernel writes the rootfs itself and then re-reads it from flash**. The NAND hardware is provably fine. This points to a bug in the kernel `hifmc100` SPI-NAND ECC handling for the W25N01GV (classic on-die-ECC vs controller-ECC / OOB-layout problem), not to bad flash, a bad write, or a bootloader/kernel ECC-domain mismatch.

## Environment

- **SoC:** HiSilicon hi3516ev300
- **Board:** Rostelecom IPC8232SWC-WE (sensor SP2305)
- **Flash:** Winbond **W25N01GV** — `ID 0xef 0xaa 0x21`, 128 MiB SLC, page 2048, OOB 64, controller ECC 4bit/512 ("ECC provided by Flash Memory Controller")
- **Firmware:** `openipc.hi3516ev300-nand-ultimate.tgz`, OpenIPC `master+6a3cde2`, kernel **Linux 4.9.37**
- **U-Boot:** `2016.11-g131d3f2` (universal), `2016.11-gbf8b847` (nand)

## Symptom

```
UBIFS error (ubi0:0 pid N): ubifs_check_node: bad CRC: calculated 0x7d5d89cf, read 0x148ef575
UBIFS error (ubi0:0 pid N): ubifs_check_node: bad node at LEB 120:89296
        magic          0x6101831
        node_type      9 (indexing node)
UBIFS error (ubi0:0 pid N): ubifs_read_node: expected node type 9
UBIFS error (ubi0:0 pid N): ubifs_iget: failed to read inode M, error -117
UBIFS error (ubi0:0 pid N): ubifs_lookup: dead directory entry '<name>', error -117
UBIFS warning: ubifs_ro_mode: switched to read-only mode, error -117
```

- Because the corrupt node is a **UBIFS index (TNC) node**, a whole subtree of inodes becomes unreachable — the reported inode/filename varies, but the underlying bad node is always **LEB 120** (offsets ~89248–101472 across runs).
- The rootfs volume is **read-only**, yet it corrupts — so this is not a stray RW write.
- `cat /sys/class/mtd/mtd3/ecc_failures` = **0**, `corrected_bits` = **0** — the controller reports no ECC activity at all (this hisi driver does not appear to update MTD ECC stats).

## Reproduction

1. Flash `openipc.hi3516ev300-nand-ultimate` onto a W25N01GV-equipped hi3516ev300 board.
2. Boot. Rootfs mounts R/O, `majestic` starts, RTSP/HTTP come up — **appears fine**.
3. Force the kernel to re-read the rootfs from flash (defeat the page cache and UBIFS TNC cache):
   ```sh
   for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
       sync
       echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches
       find / -xdev -type f -exec cat {} + >/dev/null 2>&1
   done
   dmesg | grep -c 'UBIFS error'      # -> non-zero, e.g. 78
   dmesg | grep -c 'bad CRC'          # -> e.g. 15, all at "LEB 120"
   ```
   The bad-CRC UBIFS errors appear and the filesystem drops to read-only. On a fresh boot the first full read is often clean; the errors surface once cached znodes are evicted and the node is re-read from flash.

## Decisive diagnostics (what this is NOT)

**1. Not the NAND hardware.** From U-Boot on the exact partition:
- Read the same physical block 15×: **identical CRC every time** (no read instability / read-disturb).
- 10× {erase → write pattern → read → verify} cycles: **all pass**.
- `nand bad`: **no bad blocks**.

**2. Not the write method / not a bootloader-vs-kernel ECC domain mismatch.** The rootfs was rewritten three different ways — all corrupt identically at LEB 120:
- `nand write` from the **universal** U-Boot (verified byte-perfect on U-Boot read-back).
- `nand write` from the **nand** U-Boot (verified byte-perfect on U-Boot read-back).
- **From the running kernel itself**: NFS-booted the kernel (`init=/bin/sh`, `mtdparts=...`), then `flash_eraseall /dev/mtd3` + `nandwrite -p /dev/mtd3 rootfs.ubi`. Writer and reader are then the *same* code / same ECC — and it **still** corrupts on re-read (`drop_caches` test above).

So the kernel corrupts data **it wrote itself**, on re-read — this eliminates any u-boot-vs-kernel ECC/OOB-layout difference as the cause.

**3. The two U-Boots do read the same flash differently** (evidence of ECC-scheme sensitivity): reading the identical mtd3 contents, `crc32` = `0529bf41` (universal) vs `8d080558` (nand). This is a side note; the primary result (2) is that the kernel breaks its own writes.

## Suspected root cause

Data-pattern-dependent, silent, "same error at the same logical offset regardless of physical block" is the documented failure mode of the **W25N01GV internal (on-die) ECC** interacting badly with the controller ECC / OOB layout:

- linux-mtd: the W25N01GV internal ECC *"seems to work properly only for 512B aligned writes"*; with one specific data pattern, *"read data differed from what was written… turning off ECC allowed the original data to be read correctly."* (http://lists.infradead.org/pipermail/linux-mtd/2024-October/106485.html , https://igor-misic.blogspot.com/2020/12/winbond-nand-flash-w25n01gv-problem.html )
- General hisi hifmc guidance: having *both* on-die ECC and controller ECC active (or mismatched OOB layouts) causes exactly this; one ECC scheme must be chosen consistently.

The kernel driver **intends** to disable the chip's on-die ECC and use the FMC 4bit/512 ECC:

`drivers/mtd/nand/hifmc100/hifmc_spi_nand_ids.c` (W25N01GV entry `id = {0xef,0xaa,0x21}`, and):
```c
/* Disable chip internal ECC */
reg = spi_nand_feature_op(spi, GET_OP, FEATURE_ADDR, 0);
if (reg & FEATURE_ECC_ENABLE) {
        reg &= ~FEATURE_ECC_ENABLE;
        spi_nand_feature_op(spi, SET_OP, FEATURE_ADDR, reg);
        ...
        if (reg & FEATURE_ECC_ENABLE)
                DB_MSG("Error: Chip internal ECC disable failed!\n");
}
```

Directions worth investigating (any one may be the fix):
- **Confirm the on-die ECC is actually disabled at runtime** on this W25N01GV revision (the disable is best-effort and the "disable failed" path is only a `DB_MSG`). If it silently stays enabled, on-die + FMC dual-ECC would produce exactly this corruption.
- **OOB layout mismatch** between what nandwrite/UBIFS stores and what the FMC ECC expects for this chip.
- **Read speed:** the W25N01GV table entry uses `READ_QUAD(1, INFINITE, 104)` (104 MHz quad read). If that mode is marginal on this board, sporadic silent read errors would result; a slower/standard read mode would confirm/deny.
- Consider using the chip's **on-die ECC** (mainline registers W25N01GV as `NAND_ECCREQ(1, 512)`) instead of the FMC ECC, i.e. the opposite ECC choice.

## Impact

The `nand-ultimate` build is effectively unusable on W25N01GV hi3516ev300 cameras: it looks healthy after flashing and then silently rots the rootfs into read-only within normal runtime. No user-space reflash workaround exists (proven above — u-boot and kernel writers both fail). A kernel-side driver fix is required.

I'm happy to run targeted tests on the affected hardware (dump feature registers, try a patched read mode / ECC config, etc.) to help pin the fix.

items.title: [Contract]: Task dispute and arbitration lifecycle for CleverVault
items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds a **Task Dispute and Arbitration Lifecycle** to CleverVault, governed by a dedicated `dispute_resolver` role. A user can contest a release they believe was wrong by raising a dispute on an active task, which freezes further releases and completion until the resolver settles the still-locked funds between the user (refund) and the orchestrator (payout) — closing the trust-minimization gap for in-flight tasks.

## Related Issue

Closes [#99](https://github.com/clevercon-protocol/clevercon/issues/99)

## Changes

### ⚖️ Dispute & Arbitration Lifecycle

- **\[ADD\]** `set_dispute_resolver(env, admin, resolver)` and `get_dispute_resolver(env)`
  - Admin-only role management; a dispute can only be settled by the configured resolver.
- **\[ADD\]** `raise_dispute(env, user, task_id)`
  - User-only; marks the task disputed and freezes `release_payment`, `complete_task`, `cancel_task`, and `force_complete_stale_task` until resolved. Not gated on the pause flag so users can always lock in a complaint.
- **\[ADD\]** `resolve_dispute(env, resolver, task_id, refund_to_user, payout_to_orchestrator)`
  - Resolver-only; the split must equal the task's remaining locked amount (`plan_cost - spent`); refund goes to the user's wallet, payout to the orchestrator's, then the task is finalized through the shared `finalize_task` accounting.
- **\[ADD\]** `TaskInfo.disputed`, `TaskStatus::Disputed`, `DisputeRaisedEvent` / `DisputeResolvedEvent`, and `VaultError::{TaskDisputed, NotDisputeResolver, DisputeSplitMismatch, DisputeResolverNotSet, TaskNotDisputed}`.
- **\[MODIFY\]** `release_payment`, `complete_task`, `cancel_task`, and `force_complete_stale_task` now reject disputed tasks so only the resolver can end one.
- **\[ADD\]** `contracts/agent-vault/src/tests.rs` — happy-path split, non-resolver rejection, non-user raise, split sum-mismatch, stale-bypass prevention, pause interaction, event assertions, and accounting invariants after resolution.

## Verification Results

```
cargo test
✅ 120/120 passed

cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
✅ clean

cargo fmt --check
✅ clean
```

Acceptance Criteria | Status
--- | ---
Resolver role can be set by admin and read back | ✅ `set_dispute_resolver` / `get_dispute_resolver`
`raise_dispute` freezes releases and completion; only the user can raise | ✅ release/complete/cancel/stale all reject with `TaskDisputed`
`resolve_dispute` settles exactly the remaining locked funds, only by the resolver | ✅ split must equal `plan_cost - spent`, resolver-only
Events emitted for raise and resolve | ✅ `DisputeRaisedEvent` / `DisputeResolvedEvent`
Accounting invariants (`0 <= locked <= balance`, `active_tasks_count`) hold after resolution | ✅ verified after resolution in happy-path and claw-back tests
`cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass | ✅

items.title: [SPARK-58816][SQL] Fix INSERT with column list to resolve structs inside arrays and maps positionally
items.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?
Fix `ResolveInsertionBase` to resolve struct fields positionally at every nesting level during `INSERT INTO table (column_list)`, including structs inside `ArrayType` and `MapType`.

Fixes https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-58816

### Why are the changes needed?
`createProjectForByNameQuery` only dispatched to the rename path when the top-level column was `StructType`, and `renameFieldsInStruct` only recursed into nested `StructType` fields. Structs inside arrays and maps were left 
unrenamed, causing `TableOutputResolver` to resolve them by name instead of position — silently writing values into wrong fields when source and target field order differs.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
Yes. `INSERT INTO table (column_list)` now consistently resolves struct fields positionally at all nesting levels (direct struct, array-of-struct, map-of-struct), fixing silent data corruption when source and target field order differs.

### How was this patch tested?
Added three regression tests in `SQLInsertTestSuite` covering:
- Array-of-struct positional resolution
- Map-of-struct positional resolution
- Combined direct struct + array-of-struct + map-of-struct (exact JIRA repro)

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?
No.

items.title: Bug: AmqpMessageDecoder silently drops map keys — AmqpValue body {"a":1} decodes to [1]

milestone.title: v1.4.0
milestone.description: Performance and protocol-conformance release. The full hot-path set: frame hex logging, payload copies, AmqpDecoder allocations, lazy chunk decoding. Plus the protocol gaps (#379-#381), TLS transport (#400), the remaining bugs, and PHPDoc for the public API surface (Connection, Producer, Consumer, exceptions).

items.body:
## Description

A legal AMQP 1.0 body of type `AmqpValue` (`0x76`) containing a **map** decodes to an associative array, then `array_values()` strips the keys:

```php
$rawBody = $sections[body] ?? null;
if (is_array($rawBody)) {
    $body = array_values($rawBody);
}
```

Verified by execution: publishing `{"a":1,"b":2}` as an AmqpValue yields `Message::getBody() === [1, 2]` — no exception, no warning.

## Where
- `src/Client/AmqpMessageDecoder.php:17-19`

## Why it matters
Silent data corruption. A Java/Go client publishing map-valued `AmqpValue` bodies (idiomatic in event-driven apps) is read back by PHP consumers with **keys destroyed**. The `0x75` Data path is unaffected (it returns the raw bytes), and PHP's own `Producer::send()` never produces map bodies, which is why this is untracked.

## Suggested fix
Keep associative arrays as-is — only reindex actual lists. For example:
```php
if (is_array($rawBody)) {
    $body = array_is_list($rawBody) ? $rawBody : $rawBody; // preserve keys
}
```
Or expose the raw decoded value and let the caller decide. Add a unit test covering a map-valued AmqpValue body.

items.title: Preserve backslashes in imported tag, argument, alias, and class meta
items.body:
## ⚠️ Gated: do not merge before the wporg-developer theme is fixed

**Merging this is blocked on theme-side fixes in `wporg-developer`.** Today the
importer's unslash bug *accidentally strips* backslashes out of tag/arg/class
meta, and that accidental stripping is what currently masks several
backslash-intolerant spots in the theme. Fixing the importer alone would start
delivering backslashes to code that mishandles them, turning a silent data
corruption into a visible regression.

The theme items that must land first or simultaneously (items B1/B2/B4 in the
internal follow-ups handoff):

- **B1** — `inc/template-tags.php` calls `DevHub_Formatting::link_internal_element()`
  directly for the deprecation notice and drops the whole "Use %s instead."
  sentence when nothing links; a backslashed `@see \Some_Class` either vanishes
  or emits a wrong-post-type URL.
- **B2** — `get_used_by()` compares `_wp-parser_extends` `meta_value` against
  `post_name` with raw SQL equality, so any `\` in the stored `extends` breaks a
  parent class's "Used by" list. This is the hard constraint: **`extends` must
  stay stripped until B2 is fixed.**
- **B4** — the bare-class branch of `link_internal_element()` in
  `inc/formatting.php` uses an anchored regex plus an exact-match exception
  list, so `\WP_Query` / `\wpdb` do not link there.

## The bug

`update_post_meta()` runs its value through `wp_unslash()` →
`stripslashes_deep()`, so backslashes are eaten on write. The importer already
compensates for two things and nothing else:

- `_wp_parser_namespace` via `addslashes()`
- `_wp-parser_code_snippets` / `_wp-parser_setup_blueprints` via
  `map_deep( $value, 'wp_slash' )` (added with #258, with an explanatory comment
  and a pinning test)

Everything else is corrupted live, today, for any namespaced value:

| input | stored |
| --- | --- |
| `\Foo` | `Foo` |
| `\Foo\Bar` | `FooBar` |
| `Vendor\Foo` | `VendorFoo` |

So a `@param \Foo\Bar $x` is stored as `FooBar`.

## The fix

Apply the same `map_deep( $value, 'wp_slash' )` treatment, with a comment in the
same style, to the remaining fields:

| meta key | site |
| --- | --- |
| `_wp-parser_extends` | `Importer::import_class()` |
| `_wp-parser_implements` | `Importer::import_class()` |
| `_wp-parser_properties` | `Importer::import_class()` |
| `_wp-parser_args` | `Importer::import_item()` |
| `_wp_parser_aliases` | `Importer::import_item()` |
| `_wp-parser_tags` | `Importer::import_item()` |

`_wp_parser_namespace` is deliberately **untouched** — it is already compensated
with `addslashes()`, and slashing it again would double the separators. A new
assertion pins that it still round-trips as `Vendor\Docs`.

This is importer-side only; the exporter is not touched, so a corpus diff should
show 0 hunks.

## TDD

- `Add failing tests for backslash loss in imported meta` — RED
- `Slash imported tag, argument, alias, and class meta` — GREEN

The tests follow the existing pinning-test pattern
(`File_Import_Test::test_function_snippet_metadata_preserves_backslashes`) and
cover all three shapes — single leading backslash (`\Foo`), interior separators
(`\Foo\Bar`), and no-leading-slash namespaced (`Vendor\Foo`) — across tags
(`refers` and `param` types), argument types and defaults, aliases, `extends`,
`implements`, and property types.

RED (before the fix), showing exactly the corruption described above:

```
1) WP_Parser\Tests\File_Import_Test::test_function_tag_metadata_preserves_backslashes
-            0 => '\Foo'
-            1 => '\Foo\Bar'
-            2 => 'Vendor\Foo'
+            0 => 'Foo'
+            1 => 'FooBar'
+            2 => 'VendorFoo'

2) WP_Parser\Tests\File_Import_Test::test_function_argument_metadata_preserves_backslashes
-        'type' => '\Foo'
+        'type' => 'Foo'
...
3) WP_Parser\Tests\File_Import_Test::test_function_alias_metadata_preserves_backslashes
-    'Leading' => '\Foo'
+    'Leading' => 'Foo'
...
4) WP_Parser\Tests\File_Import_Test::test_class_metadata_preserves_backslashes
-'\Foo\Bar'
+'FooBar'

FAILURES!
Tests: 153, Assertions: 403, Failures: 4.
```

GREEN (after the fix), full suite:

```
OK (153 tests, 406 assertions)
```

## Open question — the second strip at display time

`lib/class-plugin.php:238` runs `stripslashes_deep` **again** at display time, as
the last filter in the `sanitize_argument()` chain used by `make_args_safe()`.
Whether that second strip should survive is undecided, and this PR deliberately
does not change it. Worth settling together with the theme work: with the
importer fixed, that filter is now the only remaining place that silently eats
backslashes out of argument data on the way to the template.

## Deviation from the reference implementation

An earlier local draft of this change used bare `wp_slash()` rather than
`map_deep( $value, 'wp_slash' )`, and also rewrote `_wp_parser_namespace` from
`addslashes()` to `wp_slash()`. This PR uses `map_deep()` for consistency with
the adjacent snippet/Blueprint code (it also reaches object properties, not just
array members, should any of these values ever carry decoded JSON objects), and
leaves `_wp_parser_namespace` alone. That earlier draft was also mixed with
unrelated type-rendering work; this PR contains only the meta-slashing concern.

## Not included

The `--env-cwd` hardcoding in `package.json` breaks `npm run test:phpunit` from
any worktree not literally named `phpdoc-parser`. That is fixed separately in
#276 and is deliberately not part of this branch.
